formatear-json.title: JSON Formatter
formatear-json.description: Format messy or minified JSON into readable, indented text, or compress it back into a single line, all inside your browser.
formatear-json.cta: Need tools for working with APIs or data on a regular basis? We can build one for you, tailored to your workflow.
formatear-json.seoTitle: Free Online JSON Formatter & Beautifier | SonhoLab
formatear-json.seoDescription: Format minified or messy JSON into readable text in seconds, or minify it back down to a single line. Free, no signup, nothing ever leaves your browser.
formatear-json.intro: When you're working with an API response, a config file, or data that came from somewhere else, you often end up with minified JSON: everything squeezed onto a single line, impossible to read at a glance. This tool reformats it with proper indentation and line breaks so you can actually read it, and it also does the reverse: it compresses a nicely formatted JSON file down into one compact line when that's what you need.
formatear-json.step1Text: Copy the JSON text, minified or just messy, and paste it into the text box. It doesn't need to be in any particular shape — the tool processes it exactly as it comes.
formatear-json.step2Text: Click 'Format' to lay it out with two-space indentation and line breaks, or click 'Minify' for the opposite: everything collapsed into a single line.
formatear-json.step3Text: The processed JSON appears instantly, ready to copy with one click and paste wherever you need it — your code editor, your documentation, or a config file.
formatear-json.useCase1: An API returns its response as a wall of minified text, and you need to read it clearly to find a specific field or track down a bug.
formatear-json.useCase2: Someone sent you a config JSON copied from a chat or forum thread, all squeezed onto one line, and you want to review it before dropping it into your project.
formatear-json.useCase3: You have a nicely formatted JSON file in your editor and need to compress it into a single line to paste into an environment variable or shrink a file's size.
formatear-json.faq1q: Does the JSON I paste get uploaded to a server?
formatear-json.faq1a: No. All the processing happens in your browser using JavaScript: the text never travels over the internet and is never stored anywhere. Close the tab and it's gone for good.
formatear-json.faq2q: Why does it say my JSON is invalid when I copied it from a real API?
formatear-json.faq2a: This tool can only format JSON that's already syntactically valid. Common mistakes like a trailing comma, an unquoted key, or a missing quotation mark will make parsing fail, and the tool shows you the exact error message and where in the text the problem is — but it won't fix it for you automatically.
formatear-json.faq3q: Is the JSON formatter free, and is there a usage limit?
formatear-json.faq3a: Yes, it's free with no limit on how many times you use it: since nothing gets uploaded to a server, there's no cost to pass on to you. We don't ask for sign-up or an email address either.
formatear-json.faq4q: What's the difference between formatting and minifying?
formatear-json.faq4a: Formatting adds two-space indentation and line breaks so the JSON is easy to read. Minifying does the opposite: it strips out every unnecessary space and line break to collapse it into one compact line, which is handy when file size matters.
formatear-json.faq5q: Can it fix a JSON file that has syntax errors?
formatear-json.faq5a: No. The tool detects and describes the error, but it won't guess at or automatically fix a trailing comma, a missing quote, or an unquoted key. You'll need to correct the text by hand and try again.
